s1.syndrome_frame: Fetal neurological abnormalities with ventriculomegaly and irregular ventricular walls
salient_findings: Multiple hyperechoic regions within the ventricular lumens
key_facts: Normal middle cerebral artery perfusion on fetal Doppler ultrasound
Bilateral ventricular enlargement on fetal MRI
Areas of high signal intensity on T1-weighted images and low signal intensity on T2-weighted images within the ventricles
Comprehensive workup returned within normal limits

raw.syndrome_frame: Fetal neurological abnormalities with ventriculomegaly and irregular ventricular walls
salient_findings: Multiple hyperechoic regions within the ventricular lumens
key_facts: Normal middle cerebral artery perfusion on fetal Doppler ultrasound
Bilateral ventricular enlargement on fetal MRI
Areas of high signal intensity on T1-weighted images and low signal intensity on T2-weighted images within the ventricles
Comprehensive workup returned within normal limits

shortlist.label: Congenital Cytomegalovirus Infection
shortlist.why_kept: common cause of fetal neurological abnormalities and ventriculomegaly

shortlist.label: Congenital Toxoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: classic cause of fetal ventriculomegaly and intracranial calcifications

shortlist.label: Aicardi-Goutieres Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: rare genetic disorder with similar fetal MRI findings

shortlist.label: Cobblestone Lissencephaly
shortlist.why_kept: characterized by irregular ventricular walls and abnormal brain development

shortlist.label: Dandy-Walker Malformation
shortlist.why_kept: common cause of fetal ventriculomegaly and cerebellar hypoplasia

shortlist.label: Walker-Warburg Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: rare genetic disorder with similar fetal neurological abnormalities

shortlist.label: Muscle-Eye-Brain Disease
shortlist.why_kept: rare genetic disorder with similar fetal neurological and ocular findings

shortlist.label: Fetal Stroke
shortlist.why_kept: possible cause of fetal ventriculomegaly and abnormal signal intensity on MRI

raw.rationale: The presence of bilateral ventriculomegaly, irregular ventricular walls, and multiple hyperechoic regions within the ventricular lumens on ultrasound, along with areas of high signal intensity on T1-weighted images and low signal intensity on T2-weighted images within the ventricles on MRI, are consistent with the findings of congenital CMV infection, which can cause ventriculomegaly and periventricular calcifications.

rejected.label: Congenital Toxoplasmosis
rejected.why: While congenital toxoplasmosis can cause similar ultrasound findings, the normal comprehensive workup, including a TORCH panel, makes this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Aicardi-Goutieres Syndrome
rejected.why: This syndrome typically presents with more severe neurological abnormalities and systemic symptoms, which are not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Cobblestone Lissencephaly
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by a cobblestone appearance of the brain surface on imaging, which is not described in the vignette.

rejected.label: Dandy-Walker Malformation
rejected.why: This malformation typically involves hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis and cystic dilation of the fourth ventricle, which are not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Walker-Warburg Syndrome
rejected.why: This syndrome typically presents with more severe muscular and ocular abnormalities, which are not described in the vignette.

rejected.label: Muscle-Eye-Brain Disease
rejected.why: This disease typically presents with significant muscular and ocular abnormalities, which are not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Fetal Stroke
rejected.why: While fetal stroke can cause ventriculomegaly, the presence of multiple hyperechoic regions within the ventricular lumens and the roughened-appearing choroid plexus on ultrasound are more suggestive of an infectious or inflammatory process, such as congenital CMV infection.
